sections.html:
Herriman is a city in the southwest corner of Salt Lake County, bordered by Riverton to the east, South Jordan to the north and Bluffdale to the southeast. It covers about 23 square miles at roughly 5,000 feet of elevation.

The city has no post office of its own. Mail goes through the Riverton Post Office at 12760 S 2080 W, so check that closing documents use the right address. City Hall is at 5355 West Herriman Main Street, and the offices are open 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. on weekdays.

sections.h2: How fast did Herriman grow, and what does that mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Herriman grew from 1,523 residents in 2000 to 21,785 in 2010 and 55,144 in 2020, and the Census Bureau estimates 63,282 as of July 1, 2025. That jump moved the city from the 111th-largest incorporated place in Utah to the 14th-largest in two decades.

Most of the housing here is therefore recent. A development company, Rosecrest, drove much of the early building, and in 2007 a lawsuit let the city annex about 4,000 acres from Bluffdale. The city kept annexing, most recently the 933-acre Olympia development in 2022.

For a seller, newer construction usually means fewer old-house surprises. A house that needs work, or has a tenant or a title problem, is the kind of listing a financed buyer tends to pass over.

sections.h2: What is the history of Herriman?
sections.html:
The settlement dates to 1851, when Henry Harriman, Thomas Jefferson Butterfield, John Jay Stocking and Robert Cowan Petty established it. Fort Herriman stood where the community garden is today, and only two black locust trees remain from that era.

Residents petitioned for incorporation in 1999, and Herriman became a city on April 19, 2001.

sections.h2: Who provides utilities and services in Herriman?
sections.html:
Herriman City runs its own water department, while other services come from separate providers. Knowing the list helps when you transfer accounts at closing.

  • Water: the city bills around the 10th of each month and payment is due at month end. A late charge of 1.5% applies starting the second day after the due date.
  • Garbage: Wasatch Front Waste and Recycling.
  • Sewer: Jordan Basin Improvement District.
  • Fire: Unified Fire.
  • Schools: Jordan School District.

New water accounts carry a $200 deposit. It is refunded after 24 months if there are no more than two late payments, so a buyer who is new to the city may ask whether the account is in good standing.

sections.h2: What is secondary water, and does it affect the sale?
sections.html:
Secondary water is a separate pressurized irrigation line for lawns and gardens, and the Herriman City Water Department supplies it. It is usually available from early May to mid-October, then the system shuts down in stages.

To use it, a homeowner has the sprinkler connection inspected, supplies a backflow test report if the yard also runs on culinary water, and then asks the city to set a secondary meter. The city installs the meter, and a filter is recommended because the water is filtered only to 200 microns.

If your yard is still on culinary water, or the connection never passed inspection, expect a buyer or inspector to ask. It is a simple item to fix before closing, and a clean record on it avoids a delay.

sections.h2: Which schools and amenities serve Herriman?
sections.html:
Herriman public schools belong to the Jordan School District. The city has two high schools, Herriman High (opened 2010) and Mountain Ridge High (opened 2019), plus charter schools including Providence Hall and Athlos Academy.

Amenities include the Blackridge Reservoir, an ice skating facility called Ice Ribbon, a Salt Lake County recreation center, and the Zions Bank Real Academy soccer complex, whose 5,000-seat stadium is a training site for Real Salt Lake.

sections.h2: Is wildfire a concern for Herriman homeowners?
sections.html:
Yes, to a degree. Herriman is described as highly susceptible to fire because of exposed mountains, dry brush and open fields. In 2010 a fire that started during a National Guard exercise at nearby Camp Williams burned about 3,500 acres.

Utah's House Bill 48 of 2025 also led to a statewide map that scores buildings from 1 (lowest) to 8 (highest) for wildfire exposure. About 60,000 buildings statewide were placed in the high-risk group, and owners in that group may face an annual state fee once the program begins. You can search an address at wildfirerisk.utah.gov to see its score.

sections.h2: What are Herriman's rules for a basement or accessory apartment?
sections.html:
Herriman allows an internal accessory dwelling unit, called an I-ADU, only in a single-family home, and only one accessory unit is allowed per lot. The owner must live on the property, in the main house or in the unit.

  • The unit needs its own exterior entrance with a hard-surface walkway.
  • The application review fee is $559, plus a building permit fee that depends on the area remodeled.
  • Plan review takes about 7 to 14 business days.
  • The owner signs a notarized affidavit that is recorded with the County Recorder.
  • After a passed inspection and an approval letter, the owner needs a business license before renting.

The city also warns that work done without a permit may require removing finishes such as drywall and insulation for inspection. If your basement apartment was finished without paperwork, that is the cost to weigh before you list.

sections.h2: How do Herriman property taxes and recording work?
sections.html:
Herriman is in Salt Lake County, so the county sets the calendar. Valuation notices are mailed July 22, the Board of Equalization takes appeals from August 1 to September 15, tax notices go out November 1, and payment is due November 30. Unpaid current-year taxes are delinquent on December 1.

The state's 45% primary residential exemption means a home used as a primary residence is taxed on 55% of its market value. At closing, the deed is recorded by the Salt Lake County Recorder at a flat $40 fee, with no more than ten legal descriptions before extra charges apply.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Herriman?
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the lender, so the timeline depends on title work rather than on a buyer's loan approval.

  1. Send us the address and a few details.
  2. We review the house and the comparable sales nearby.
  3. You choose to accept or decline the offer.
  4. A title company clears title and sets the closing date.
  5. The deed is recorded, and you receive the proceeds from closing.

Houses with an unfinished I-ADU, a secondary water problem or a late tax bill are exactly the kind that slow a financed buyer down. We buy the house as it stands, so those items are sorted out at closing rather than before listing.

faqs.a: Salt Lake County. Herriman sits in the southwest part of the county, so the Salt Lake County assessor, treasurer and recorder handle your parcel.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Herriman?
faqs.a: November 30. Salt Lake County lists that as the last day to pay without penalty, and unpaid taxes are delinquent from December 1.

faqs.q: Can I rent out a basement apartment in Herriman?
faqs.a: Yes, if the home is a single-family house and the owner lives on the property. Herriman requires an I-ADU permit, a notarized affidavit recorded with the county, a passed final inspection and a business license before renting.
Jordan School District. Herriman has two high schools, Herriman High and Mountain Ridge High.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: The flat recording fee is $40, plus $2 for each legal description beyond ten. The document needs a notary acknowledgment and the tax serial number of each parcel.
